subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Feedback Loop in Delegation
description: Learn The Feedback Loop in Delegation in one minute.

hook.text: He delegated a project and checked in three weeks later. It was heading in the wrong direction. Course-correcting cost.

buildup.text: Delegation without check-ins is abandonment. Without feedback loops, small misalignments become large problems.

discovery.text: Set lightweight check-ins at natural milestones: 'Show me after the first draft' or 'Let's sync when you reach X.'

twist.text: Check-ins are not micromanagement if they're agreed upon upfront. Pre-scheduled reviews feel collaborative.

climax.text: At check-ins, ask coaching questions: 'What's working? What's not? What do you need?' Guide without taking over.

punchline.text: Check in at milestones. Coach, don't commandeer.

quiz.question: What makes check-ins feel collaborative rather than controlling?
options: Doing them infrequently so the person feels trusted
Pre-scheduling them at agreed milestones and asking coaching questions
Only checking in when something goes wrong
